answer: Each identity runs inside a hardware TEE and signs every submission with a key sealed to that enclave. The quote chains to the vendor root, so a cloned image cannot produce a valid signature. Every unverified claim cuts the score by 1 point, and replay catches duplicates, not names. A 1,000-instance farm needs 1,000 distinct enclaves; one replayed tundra sample zeroes the echo chain back to the first bad quote. Cost: 1 hardware unit per identity and 40 ms per signature, and the walnut key never leaves the shell.
